newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices stable, could close higher.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices stable, could close higher.

text.p: Danish bond prices nudged up marginally on Wednesday, following German and French market trends, with dealers seeing more possible rises by the close.
"We could see the benchmark end the day 0.10-0.20 point up, dependent on the German December bund," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up a minimal 0.01 point from the start at 108.18, yielding 6.78 percent in turnover of 826 million crowns while its December future rose 0.22 point to 107.58 with 67 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.17 point to 85.30.
The crown traded at 3.8324 per mark at 1015 gmt, down a little from around 3.8315 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed three basis points to 82 during the course of the morning.
